name: Centaur, Mudosan
body:
Tauric creatures exist in many of the different realities that make up the shattered worlds. On some, they may not even resemble the traditional understanding of what a centaur is, but to the denizens there, they are one and the same.

Society Mudosans roamed their homeworld in herds until advancing technology and modernization slowly wore them down to the point where most settled into families to survive. Those who travel to the Collective and beyond sometimes retain a sense of their ancestors’ past, while others prefer to draw little attention to their history and blend in the local region’s inhabitants instead.

Relations: Mudosans enjoy the company of anybody who appreciates the natural world and the outdoors. They instinctively dislike those who seek to push technological advancements that go against the natural order, but will work with inventors and similar creatives to find appropriate alternatives when able.

Alignment and Religion: Mudosans are a spiritual people, believing deeply in the spirits of their ancestors and the world at large. Most keep shrines honoring past family members, and will defend their family’s ways, even if it comes to bloodshed.

Adventurers: By the age of 15, most young mudosan have a good bearing on what they hope to accomplish when they come of age. This allows them to begin training as adventurers as early as humans, despite not reaching physical maturity until 30. Mudosans honoring their past will take on roles such as barbarian, cleric, druid, or ranger; whereas more independent mudosans have been known to become fighters, paladins, and shifters. A rare few take on bloodlines as sorcerers, and fewer still go against their ancestral ways completely to pursue life as gunslingers or inventors.

Mudosan Names: Mudosans take on variations of names they’ve heard others use while growing up, sometimes developing their name over several years before settling on a one or two-syllable monicker by which to go by.

Example Names: Enrol, Lanng, Stefe, Wareth

Mudosan Centaurs

The mudosan are powerful, even for centaurs. On their world, they are revered as guardians and protectors. For ages, they have lived up to that role, but not all seek to be praised for the accomplishments of their ancestors.

Physical Description: Mudosan have a disproportionately large torso relative to their lower body. They typically have an impressive pair of antlers surrounded by lion-like manes. Their greater upper body strength allows them to easily accomplish tasks traditional centaurs cannot.

Mudosan Ancestry Traits

All mudosans share the following traits.

Ability Score Modifiers: +4 Strength, +2 Wisdom, –2 Dexterity, –2 Intelligence. Mudosan are strong, spiritual beings, but their size and lack of modernization makes it harder to adjust to different situations.
Speed: A mudosan’s base movement is 40 feet.
Size: Large. As Large creatures, mudosans take a –1 size penalty to their AC, a –1 size penalty on attack rolls, a +1 bonus on combat maneuver checks and to their CMD, and a –4 size penalty on Stealth checks. They take up a space that is 10 feet by 10 feet and have a reach of 5 feet.
Quadruped: Mudosans possess four legs and two arms, granting them a +4 racial bonus to CMD against trip attempts. They must wield Large weapons and wear Large-sized armor.
Type: Monstrous Humanoid. Mudosans are monstrous humanoids with darkvision out to 60 feet.
Languages: Mudosans begin play speaking Common and one of the following languages of their choice. Mudosans with high Intelligence scores can choose from the same list: Dwarven, Elven, Gnomish, Halfling, Orc.
Advanced Mudosan: Mudosans sometimes grow more powerful and bestial than others of their kind. This has been attributed to various factors, including mutation, divine transformation, or a sometimes unknown heritage. Advanced mudosans gain all of the same traits as mudosans in addition to the following. Regular mudosans can select these options as ancestry feats instead, representing them growing into their traits.
Gore: Advanced mudosans are more adept at using their horns. They gain a natural gore attack that deals 1d8 damage on a hit, or double damage when they charge (this functions as a lance).
Natural Armor: An (advanced) mudosan gains +2 natural armor bonus due to its thicker hide.
Two-Foot Mudosan Ancestry Traits

Two-feet are mudosans whose back legs have been removed. Some mudosan choose this in order to further distance themselves from their ancestors, or as a form of sacrifice to draw less attention to themselves. Whatever the reason, the physical change also causes their bodies to take on their advanced form to make up for any sudden deficiencies. Two-foot mudosans have the following ancestry traits.

Ability Score Modifiers: +2 Strength, +2 Wisdom, –2 Dexterity or Intelligence. Two-feet’s torsos remain strong. During their recovery, they may put more emphasis on mobility or education.
Speed: A two-foot’s base movement is 30 feet.
Sprinter: Two-feet gain a +10 foot racial bonus to their speed when using the charge, run, or withdraw actions.
Size: Medium. A two-foot’s frame is still bigger than most creatures, but without its hind legs, its size is Medium. It receives no bonuses or penalties due to its size.
Type: Monstrous Humanoid. Two-feet are still monstrous humanoids that gain darkvision out to 60 feet.
Advanced Mudosan: Two-feet have both the gore attack and the natural armor granted to advanced mudosans.
Oversized: A two-foot mudosan still has the torso of a gorilla, which means it still must wield Large weapons and wear armor sized for a Large creature.
Languages: Two-foot mudosans spend much of their recovery time learning more about the world around them. They begin play with the same languages as mudosans, but those with high Intelligence scores can choose any languages they want (except secret languages, such as Druidic).
Mudosan Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian: Gain a +1/3 bonus on critical hit confirmation rolls with the barbarian’s gore attack (maximum bonus of +5). This bonus does not stack with those gained through Critical Focus and similar effects.
Bard: Add one spell known from the druid’s spell list. This spell must be at least one level below the highest spell level the bard can cast. The spell is treated as being one level higher, unless it is also on the bard spell list.
Cleric: Select one domain power granted at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + the cleric’s Wisdom modifier. The cleric adds +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that domain power.
Druid: Add +1 to the druid’s base speed. In combat this option has no effect unless the druid has selected it five times (or another increment of five). This bonus stacks with the monk’s fast movement class feature and applies under the same conditions as that feature.
Fighter: Gain a +1/3 bonus on critical hit confirmation rolls with the barbarian’s gore attack (maximum bonus of +5). This bonus does not stack with those gained through Critical Focus and similar effects.
Gunslinger: Add +1/4 to the dodge bonus to AC granted by the nimble class feature (maximum +2) or +1/4 to the AC bonus gained when using the gunslinger’s dodge deed.
Inventor: Gain a +1/2 bonus on checks used to Appraise or Craft objects made of wood, a +1/2 bonus on Disable Device checks regarding wooden traps and a +1/2 bonus to AC and Reflex saves against wooden traps.
Paladin: Add +1/6 to the morale bonus on saving throws provided by the paladin’s auras.
Ranger: Add a +1/2 bonus on wild empathy checks to influence animals and magical beasts that live on plains.
Shifter: Gain a +1/3 bonus on critical hit confirmation rolls with the shifter’s gore attack (maximum bonus of +5). This bonus does not stack with those gained through Critical Focus and similar effects.
Sorcerer: Add one spell known from the druid’s spell list. This spell must be at least one level below the highest spell level the sorcerer can cast. The spell is treated as being one level higher, unless it is also on the sorcerer spell list.
Mudosan Living Ammunition

The creatures of mudos grow their ammunition live; adapting their ranged weapons to make use of the naturally dangerous insects and other tiny animals that exist there. The mudosans prefer this to manufacturing wasteful ammunition from limited resources such as metal.

Using Living Ammunition: Loading a weapon with living ammunition requires a successful Handle Animal check at the listed DC. Failure means the action is lost and must be attempted again. Failure by 5 or more means the ammunition got away before it could be loaded.
